SLE with multiple joint pains\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003Eb)\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003EWhat is the etiology of the current problem and how would you as a member of the treating team arrive at a diagnosis?\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003EPlease chart out the sequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of her problems and current outcomes.\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAccording to the patient history,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003Ethe etiology\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003Emycobacterium tuberculosis\u003C\/b\u003E,also the CBNAAT done for csf is\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003Epositive\u003C\/b\u003E,indicating\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003ETubercular meningitis\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003ETo arrive at a diagnosis,for chronic headache CT or MRI is the preferred modality,\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EMRI was done and it revealed\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003Efocal acute infarcts\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;in the left thalamus.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EAlso lumbar puncture was done it revealed normal protein and cell count but the glucose levels were decreased.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003Esequence of events\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgPvZYu3962rRFOK29DR6W9tWAp0eYhUPL7zh9lDM8EVUE_2HBGmcFidia7AnTl9l2tW9xnAjizuElpD54MXN-TjTeIDFwOyTT7HHfeOAPIlg4oinmXZCInw98IgoQS-oOZoRx1jXiSdm4\/s1600\/1611301246097087-1.png\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgPvZYu3962rRFOK29DR6W9tWAp0eYhUPL7zh9lDM8EVUE_2HBGmcFidia7AnTl9l2tW9xnAjizuElpD54MXN-TjTeIDFwOyTT7HHfeOAPIlg4oinmXZCInw98IgoQS-oOZoRx1jXiSdm4\/s1600\/1611301246097087-1.png\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003ETubercular meningitis (TBM) is a rare condition in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The aim of this study is to describe the clinical characteristics, possible risk factors, and outcomes of SLE patients with TBM.\u0026nbsp;On systematically reviewing medical records from10 SLE patients with TBM admitted to a hospital from December 2008 to December 2018. A total of 100 cases in the same period were randomly selected as controls from SLE inpatients without infection. In patients with TBM, the mean age at presentation was 35.2\u0026nbsp;years (range 19.8–45.2); the mean duration of SLE was 34.6\u0026nbsp;months (range 4–84\u0026nbsp;months).\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u0026nbsp;Patients with TBM had significantly longer SLE duration, higher ESR and CRP level, and lower CD4+ cell counts and albumin level than those without infections (\u003Ci\u003Ep\u003C\/i\u003E \u0026lt; 0.05 for all). There were no differences in prednisone dose at the time of symptom onset or cumulative dose over the preceding year between the two groups. Logistic regression analysis showed that patients with a lower CD4+ cell count were more likely to have TBM compared with controls (OR = 3.67,\u0026nbsp;\u003Ci\u003Ep\u003C\/i\u003E = 0.020).\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003ETBM should be considered when SLE patients have central nervous system (CNS) symptoms with a longer duration, higher ESR and CRP level, and lower CD4+ cell counts and albumin level, even if the patients are receiving a low prednisone dose,and the patient being studied has a chronic headache and fits into this criteria\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ec) What is the efficacy of each of the drugs listed in her prior treatment plan that she was following since last two years before she stopped it two weeks back?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E. Hydroxychloroquine\u003Cbr\u003E.sulfasalazine\u003Cbr\u003E. methylprednisolone\u003Cbr\u003E.aceclofenac\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E. cholecalciferol\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E.alandronic acid\u003Cbr\u003E. flupirtine\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E. gabapentin\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E. methylcobalamine tablets.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cb\u003EWhy was she given bisphosphonates?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003EHydroxychloroquine in SLE\u003Cbr\u003E“Chloroquine, together with its hydroxyl derivative hydroxychloroquine, was initially used as an antimalarial agent, but is also useful in the treatment of autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E• Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine are approved for the treatment of SLE and have been shown to reduce the frequency of disease flares (particularly of lupus nephritis),\u0026nbsp;contribute to the maintenance of remission, prolong the onset of disease and reduce the risk of complications.Beyond their immunomodulatory effects in SLE, these agents have also been shown to protect against thrombotic events,\u0026nbsp;improve glucose and lipid profiles, and prevent renal damage,apparently resulting in reduced cardiovascular risk, for which SLE is an independent risk factor”\u003Cbr\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7097534\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7097534\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E2)sulfasalazine\u003Cbr\u003EImmunosuppressive drug used in the treatment of cutaneous manifestations of lupus.\u003Cbr\u003E“Sulfasalazine\u0026nbsp;is an effective agent for\u0026nbsp;chronic discoid lupus erythematosus\u0026nbsp;(CDLE) but the response to treatment is considerably variable between patients and is also unpredictable. The reason for this might relate to differences in metabolism of the drug which is extensively acetylated by the polymorphic enzyme N-acetyltransferase 2 (NAT2). To test this possibility, the N-acetylation phenotype of eleven patients with CDLE and treated by standard doses of\u0026nbsp;sulfasalazine\u0026nbsp;was retrospectively determined by genotyping. A clear-cut difference in the outcome of treatment was observed according to whether the patients were slow acetylators (SA) or rapid acetylators (RA). Eight out of 11 patients responded to treatment with a complete or marked remission of the disease. Seven of them were RA. The three other patients who did not respond at all to the drug were SA. In addition, SA seem to be more prone to toxic events. These findings strongly suggest that the genetic polymorphism of\u0026nbsp;NAT2\u0026nbsp;is responsible for differences in the response to\u0026nbsp;sulfasalazine\u0026nbsp;in patients with CDLE. Therefore, candidates for\u0026nbsp;sulfasalazine\u0026nbsp;therapy should be genotyped to identify those patients who might benefit from the drug.”\u003Cbr\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/journals.lww.com\/jpharmacogenetics\/Abstract\/1997\/04000\/NAT2_genotyping_and_efficacy_of_sulfasalazine_in.6.aspx\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/journals.lww.com\/jpharmacogenetics\/Abstract\/1997\/04000\/NAT2_genotyping_and_efficacy_of_sulfasalazine_in.6.aspx\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3) Please critically appraise the full text article linked below:\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Ca data-saferedirecturl=\"https:\/\/www.google.com\/url?hl=en\u0026amp;q=https:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1111\/j.1365-2796.2003.01233.x\u0026amp;source=gmail\u0026amp;ust=1610125321028000\u0026amp;usg=AFQjCNHXD3ybzJ24LAs7F9GDZ3oIliRmEw\" href=\"https:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1111\/j.1365-2796.2003.01233.x\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.\u003Cwbr\u003Ecom\/doi\/full\/10.1111\/j.1365-\u003Cwbr\u003E2796.2003.01233.x\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EWhat is the efficacy of aspirin in stroke in your assessment of the evidence provided in the article. The progression rate was 15.9% amongst patients treated with aspirin and 16.7% for those on placebo.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EThe ability to live at home, to walk unaided, or need for further institutionalized care after discharge was not significantly improved in the aspirin group .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERCT CASP checklist:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/documentcloud.adobe.com\/link\/review?uri=urn:aaid:scds:US:8d251179-8d1c-435c-803e-0daf96229a3f\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/documentcloud.adobe.com\/link\/review?uri=urn:aaid:scds:US:8d251179-8d1c-435c-803e-0daf96229a3f\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4) Please mention your individual learning experiences from this month.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli\u003EHypothyroidism and kidney failure\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003ECLD with portal HTN secondary to ?
